title: Start with what you need
selection_rules: Interpret the requested outcome, available artifacts, accepted decisions and authority semantically; do not route from keywords or regex matches alone.
Choose one first missing job and explain why, its expected artifact and the next conditional handoff. Reuse current accepted work rather than recreating it.
An explicit named skill or scoped direct request takes precedence over advisory suggestions. Do not hijack unrelated work with a universal Core-first workflow.

Use this compact set for common starts. In source context consult the existing skill-job map for current catalog names; in verified runtime context use the available skill inventory and relevant bundled capability descriptor. Read the selected installed skill entry and only needed resources.
Ask only for missing information that changes the route. Missing competing inputs stay missing; do not fabricate proposals, evidence, acceptance or completion.
Steps are conditional choices, not automatic invocation or execution. A missing document does not establish a missing decision. UI state selections are user-provided context, not verified acceptance.
Preserve user, host, home and project policy. Routing grants no new permission. Proceed within an already authorized task without re-asking permission merely to select the skill.

Supercharge, continuity, goal-packet compilation and Batman are optional explicit requests. A goal packet does not launch a goal; delegation and external actions retain their existing authority gates.

When the next job or depth is materially unclear, the available intake skill explains options and asks adaptive questions; every question supports Other/free text. Clear direct tasks skip the interview. Relationships may sequence, iterate, return, support or conditionally parallelize work; none grants execution authority.

routes.title: Other — help me find the right job
routes.intent: The desired job, starting point or useful depth is uncertain; describe it in your own words.
routes.why: The assistant interprets the current context across the whole catalog rather than making you choose a framework.
routes.output: One justified next job and depth, or a focused question with Other/free text.

steps.label: Clarify the useful next job
steps.when: A missing answer would materially change the next result or depth.
steps.skip_when: The direct task or selected skill is already clear.
steps.output: A context-based recommendation, expected artifact and necessary clarification.
steps.next: Read the selected current contract and continue already authorized work; preserve actual prerequisites and approval holds.

routes.prompt: Use the available intake skill to recommend the next useful job from my context. If a material uncertainty remains, explain the relevant outcome options, recommend one with a reason and ask a focused question using an available question tool or inline options. Always include Other/free text. Do not require me to choose a framework or invent an appetite.
routes.next: Continue with the selected current skill only within established scope; do not automatically run a stack.

routes.title: I have a rough problem
routes.intent: The problem, affected people or desired outcome is still vague.
routes.why: Clarify the problem before choosing a solution.
routes.output: A solution-free frame with outcome, appetite and answerable uncertainties.

steps.label: Frame the problem
steps.when: The problem or outcome is not yet clear.
steps.skip_when: A current accepted frame already answers these questions.
steps.output: A solution-free frame with affected people, desired outcome, actual appetite and open questions.
steps.next: After the owner accepts the frame, specify a concrete change if acceptance needs definition, or choose a full shaping workshop if requested.

steps.label: Define behavior and acceptance
steps.when: Feature behavior or acceptance is unclear.
steps.skip_when: Accepted requirements already cover this change.
steps.output: Requirements, observable acceptance checks, unchanged behavior and unresolved owner decisions.
steps.next: Once requirements are accepted, resolve any material technical choice; otherwise plan useful tasks or implement an already authorized bounded change.

routes.prompt: Help me clarify [problem or rough idea] for [people/context]. Identify the outcome, appetite and questions that matter before proposing a solution. Use what we already know; do not invent decisions.
routes.next: After the owner accepts the frame, specify a concrete change if acceptance needs definition, or choose a full shaping workshop if that is the requested job.

routes.title: I know the feature, but not acceptance
routes.intent: The desired feature/change is identifiable, but its observable behavior or acceptance conditions are unclear.
routes.why: Define what success means before breaking work down.
routes.output: Source-backed requirements, acceptance checks, unchanged behavior and open decisions.

steps.label: Define behavior and acceptance
steps.when: Feature behavior or acceptance is unclear.
steps.skip_when: Accepted requirements already cover this change.
steps.output: Requirements, observable acceptance checks, unchanged behavior and unresolved owner decisions.
steps.next: Once requirements are accepted, resolve any material technical choice; otherwise plan useful tasks or implement an already authorized bounded change.

steps.label: Resolve a material design choice
steps.when: A material technical choice remains after requirements are understood.
steps.skip_when: No material design choice remains; a missing architecture document alone is not a reason to add this step.
steps.output: A justified design decision with alternatives, interfaces, failure modes, migration and rollback.
steps.next: Return requirement changes to their owner. Use accepted design for task planning only when breakdown helps, or for an already authorized bounded implementation.

steps.label: Break accepted work into tasks
steps.when: Accepted scope benefits from several independently verifiable tasks.
steps.skip_when: The authorized change is already one bounded task, or an accepted task plan remains current.
steps.output: Verifiable tasks with dependencies, consumed and produced interfaces, checks, allowed writes and unresolved holds.
steps.next: Select the next authorized bounded slice; planning alone starts neither implementation nor a goal.

steps.label: Implement one authorized slice
steps.when: A bounded change and its edit/check authority are established.
steps.skip_when: The requested scope is analysis only, or the actual slice is already implemented.
steps.output: A focused patch, actual verification results and remaining limits for the authorized slice.
steps.next: Review the actual candidate as required. Keep subsequent repairs and hosted delivery within their existing authorization.

steps.label: Review the actual candidate
steps.when: A real diff, commit or candidate needs judgment under the applicable review rules.
steps.skip_when: The requested deliverable has no candidate, or valid review already covers the exact unchanged candidate; never waive a required review.
steps.output: Actionable findings tied to the exact candidate, with reviewed coverage and limits.
steps.next: Apply selected actionable comments only when authorized, then re-review. If no repairs remain, assess the requested delivery gate without inferring merge or publication authority.

routes.prompt: Define the behavior and acceptance conditions for [feature/change] from [notes/sources]. Preserve [existing behavior]. Reuse accepted decisions and make open questions explicit. Return a specification; do not implement yet.
routes.next: Once requirements are accepted, use architecture only for a remaining material decision; otherwise plan useful tasks or implement an already authorized bounded change.

routes.title: I need to choose between proposals
routes.intent: Two or more actual proposals, drafts or sources disagree and a recommendation is wanted.
routes.why: Compare the supplied alternatives and expose conflicts instead of blending incompatible ideas.
routes.output: An attributed comparison, trade-offs, rejected alternatives and a defensible recommendation.

steps.label: Reconcile actual alternatives
steps.when: Competing inputs and decision criteria are available.
steps.skip_when: The choice is already settled, or no competing inputs exist; request missing inputs instead of inventing alternatives.
steps.output: An attributed comparison, conflicts, trade-offs, rejected alternatives and one defensible recommendation.
steps.next: The owner resolves the decision. Carry the accepted choice to architecture, specification or planning only if that work remains.

routes.prompt: Compare [actual proposal A] and [actual proposal B] using [decision criteria]. Explain conflicts, trade-offs and rejected ideas, then recommend one. If an input is missing, ask for it rather than inventing its content.
routes.next: Carry the accepted decision to architecture, specification or planning only if that work remains; a recommendation does not make the human decision.

routes.title: I want a full Shape Up workshop
routes.intent: The user explicitly wants guided framing, research, shaping and pitch preparation through a human betting decision.
routes.why: Keep stage evidence and human decisions with the shaping conductor.
routes.output: A reviewed shaping bundle and an explicit human betting decision or hold.

steps.label: Frame the problem and appetite
steps.when: A full workshop is requested and current G0/G1 framing evidence plus actual engineering acceptance are not established.
steps.skip_when: The current frame, real appetite, G0/G1 evidence and required human acceptance are established.
steps.output: A solution-free frame, actual appetite, G0/G1 evidence and recorded human acceptance status.
steps.next: Begin Research only after current framing gates, engineering agreement and required answers are established. An explicit frame-only request stops at its accepted boundary.

steps.label: Resolve material uncertainties
steps.when: The accepted frame has material questions or lacks current G2 research evidence.
steps.skip_when: Current G2 evidence resolves the relevant stage questions; never invent research.
steps.output: Source-backed findings that answer the stage questions, with coverage limits, unresolved uncertainties and current G2 evidence or hold.
steps.next: Shape a bounded solution only when current G2 prerequisites are met; material missing evidence remains in Research.

steps.label: Shape a bounded solution
steps.when: Accepted framing and current research support shaping within the actual appetite.
steps.skip_when: A current shaped solution and all required diagrams/contracts are ready for review.
steps.output: A bounded shaped candidate with required diagrams, interface and security contracts, risks and unresolved decisions.
steps.next: Carry the current packet to author audit and independent G3 review. Reopen Research or Framed when material uncertainty or scope changes require it.

steps.label: Review the shaped packet
steps.when: The current shaped packet needs the conductor review route, independent review and G3 evidence.
steps.skip_when: Valid G3 evidence covers the unchanged packet; a standalone pitch review does not fabricate workshop receipts.
steps.output: Independent findings and repair dispositions tied to the shaped packet, with current G3 evidence or a review hold.
steps.next: Draft-only work stops at its accepted G3 boundary. Otherwise obtain actual team acceptance and complete approved target delivery before treating the package as ready for betting.

steps.label: Verify authorized delivery and stage readiness
steps.when: Betting is in scope and approved targets or current G4 evidence remain incomplete.
steps.skip_when: Draft-only scope stops at its accepted boundary, or required targets and current G4 evidence are already verified.
steps.output: Verified saved-target readback and current G4 evidence, or a concrete delivery hold.
steps.next: After current G3 evidence, actual team acceptance and applicable G4 checks, the human owner bets, sends back, abandons or splits; only accepted and authorized scope can hand off.

routes.prompt: Guide a full Shape Up workshop for [problem] within [actual appetite]. Resume at the first unaccepted stage. Carry real framing, research, shaping and pitch evidence through the required reviews and gates; leave the betting decision to the human owner.
routes.next: After current G3 evidence, actual team acceptance and applicable G4 delivery checks, the human owner bets, sends back, abandons or splits. Only accepted and authorized build scope can hand off; the conductor preserves all earlier stage gates.

steps.when: The cause or safe repair boundary is unknown.

steps.output: Reproduction and discriminating evidence supporting a scoped cause or honest unknown, plus the proposed repair boundary.
steps.next: Implement a supported bounded repair when authorized; otherwise stop with the cause or missing observation. A passing retry alone proves neither cause nor fix.

routes.title: I have a diff to review
routes.intent: The requested deliverable is judgment of an actual diff, commit or pull/merge request.
routes.why: Review the supplied candidate directly instead of rebuilding its upstream process.
routes.output: Actionable findings tied to the exact candidate, with coverage and limits.

steps.label: Review the actual candidate

routes.prompt: Review [exact diff/commit/PR/MR] for correctness, scope and regressions. Tie findings to the candidate and state coverage limits. Do not edit or post externally unless my request authorizes it.
routes.next: Selected actionable comments go to the feedback-repair job, then re-review; no broad refactor is implied.

routes.title: I have a pitch to review
routes.intent: The requested deliverable is assessment or improvement of a finished pitch.
routes.why: Assess the real pitch without fabricating prior workshop stages.
routes.output: A scored pitch review, gaps, risks and betting-readiness recommendation.

steps.label: Review the supplied pitch
steps.when: A pitch is available and needs assessment.
steps.skip_when: A current accepted review covers the unchanged pitch.
steps.output: A pitch assessment with evidence-backed gaps, risks and a betting-readiness recommendation.
steps.next: The owner resolves material gaps and makes the betting decision; review does not create workshop history or implementation authority.

routes.prompt: Review [pitch] against its problem, actual appetite, solution, risks and evidence. Identify gaps and improve the artifact within [scope]. Do not invent workshop history or a human betting decision.
routes.next: The owner resolves material gaps and makes the betting decision; a source review is not implementation or release evidence.

routes.title: I explicitly want to strengthen an artifact
routes.intent: A prompt, plan or proposal needs an explicitly requested stress test.
routes.why: This optional job is selected only when explicitly requested.
routes.output: A stronger artifact with assumptions and failure modes.

steps.label: I explicitly want to strengthen an artifact
steps.when: A prompt, plan or proposal needs an explicitly requested stress test.
steps.skip_when: The job was not explicitly requested, or a current accepted artifact already satisfies it.
steps.output: A stronger artifact with assumptions and failure modes.
steps.next: Use the improved artifact only within its existing authority.

routes.prompt: Strengthen [prompt/plan/proposal] for [goal] while preserving its scope and authority. Do not execute its target.
routes.next: Use the improved artifact only within its existing authority.

routes.title: I explicitly need continuity
routes.intent: A long investigation needs a durable, source-backed handoff.
routes.why: This optional job is selected only when explicitly requested.
routes.output: Verified context, decisions, pending work and evidence references.

steps.output: Verified context, decisions, pending work and evidence references.
steps.next: Resume from verified state; saved context is not proof that pending work completed.

routes.prompt: Preserve a resumable handoff for [investigation] in [authorized project location]. Distinguish verified facts, decisions and open work. Do not write global memory.
routes.next: Resume from verified state; saved context is not proof that pending work completed.

routes.prompt: Use Batman orchestration for [accepted scope] within [allowed actions and budget]. Follow its required independent-review and delivery gates. Do not infer merge, release or installation authority beyond my request.

questions.question: What would be most useful to leave this conversation with?
questions.why: Choose the result you need, not a framework name. Your assistant can recommend an option from the context you already gave.

options.label: A clearer problem or feature
options.detail: Understand what matters before choosing a solution.

options.label: A recommendation between actual alternatives
options.detail: Compare proposals you already have.
options.rationale: Converge compares real alternatives and explains trade-offs; it does not invent missing proposals.

options.label: A proposal others can judge or fund
options.detail: Develop a justified pitch, or assess one that exists.

options.label: Working code, a fix or an implementation plan
options.detail: Start from the actual work and decisions already accepted.

options.label: I am not sure—help me decide
options.detail: Ask me a focused question about my situation.
options.rationale: There is not enough information for a responsible skill recommendation. The assistant should ask about your desired outcome and what you already have.

options.label: Other — describe what you mean
options.detail: Enter your own answer; the assistant will interpret it.
options.rationale: A free-form answer needs context-sensitive interpretation. Ask a useful follow-up instead of forcing it into an existing choice.

questions.question: Which part is unclear?
questions.why: An unclear problem and unclear feature behavior need different first steps.

options.label: Why this matters, for whom, or what success means
options.detail: We have symptoms or rough ideas, not an agreed problem.
options.rationale: Start with lightweight framing. It clarifies the problem; it does not commit you to a full workshop.

options.label: The feature is known, but its behavior is unclear
options.detail: We need observable requirements and acceptance conditions.
options.rationale: Specification fits an identifiable change whose expected behavior still needs agreement.

options.label: I cannot tell yet
options.detail: Help me distinguish the uncertainty.
options.rationale: The assistant should use your examples to distinguish the problem from its proposed solution before selecting a skill.

options.label: Other — describe what you mean
options.detail: Enter your own answer; the assistant will interpret it.
options.rationale: A free-form answer needs context-sensitive interpretation. Ask a useful follow-up instead of forcing it into an existing choice.

questions.question: What do you already have for the proposal?
questions.why: A finished pitch can be reviewed directly. Rough material may need the guided workshop.

options.label: An existing pitch to assess
options.detail: Judge this artifact rather than restart its history.
options.rationale: Review the actual pitch directly; do not invent earlier workshop stages.

options.label: Notes or ideas that need developing into a decision-ready pitch
options.detail: Guide problem framing, research, solution shaping and review.
options.rationale: The shaping conductor matches this end-to-end outcome. It explains stages, reuses accepted work and leaves appetite and betting decisions with people.

options.label: I need help deciding how much work is worthwhile
options.detail: Discuss the decision, uncertainty and time investment first.
options.rationale: The assistant should explain a lightweight clarification versus a decision-ready workshop and recommend depth from your needs; it must not invent an appetite.

options.label: Other — describe what you mean
options.detail: Enter your own answer; the assistant will interpret it.
options.rationale: A free-form answer needs context-sensitive interpretation. Ask a useful follow-up instead of forcing it into an existing choice.

questions.question: Which best describes the starting point?
questions.why: Reuse accepted work. These answers are context, not proof of completion or permission.

options.label: A small, clear task or supported repair
options.detail: The change and allowed scope are already clear.
options.rationale: Implement a bounded slice without a fresh workshop or planning chain.

options.label: Accepted requirements that need task breakdown
options.detail: Plan dependencies and verifiable outcomes before execution.
options.rationale: Plan implementation from accepted scope; resolve a material technical choice only if one remains.

options.label: A feature idea with unclear expected behavior
options.detail: Agree on what it should do before planning implementation.
options.rationale: Specify acceptance and preserved behavior before breaking work into tasks.

options.label: A failure whose cause is not understood
options.detail: A test, build or runtime behavior fails unexpectedly.
options.rationale: Diagnose the cause before treating a plausible fix as supported.

options.label: Something else, or I am unsure
options.detail: Let the assistant inspect my context and ask what matters.
options.rationale: A generic questionnaire cannot settle this case. Ask the smallest useful question rather than force a route.

options.label: Other — describe what you mean
options.detail: Enter your own answer; the assistant will interpret it.
options.rationale: A free-form answer needs context-sensitive interpretation. Ask a useful follow-up instead of forcing it into an existing choice.
